seoTitle: Commit Message Suggester from a git diff (Conventional Commits)
metaDescription: Paste a unified git diff and get a Conventional Commits subject and file summary drafted from paths and changes. Heuristic, nothing uploaded.
intro: Draft a commit message from your staged changes: type, scope and a list of files with line counts.
why:
The tool reads git diff headers and hunks, counts additions and deletions per file, classifies files (tests, docs, CI, build files, styles, code) and chooses a type: test, docs, ci, build, style, fix, feat or refactor. The scope comes from the common directory of changed code files.

It is a rule-based starting point. Replace the subject with what the change does and why, add "!" or a BREAKING CHANGE footer for incompatible changes, and keep the subject under about 72 characters.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: Run git diff --staged (or git diff) and copy the output.
Paste it and read the suggested subject and file list.
Rewrite the subject to say what and why.

faq.a: No. It looks at file paths, change sizes and a few keywords. Review the type it picks.
